text:
This was a coin flip that Juuse Saros refused to let land on its edge. Nashville and Los Angeles each generated almost exactly 2.9 expected goals (the quality of chances), the Kings had 66 shot attempts to the Predators' 51, and by our replay of every shot Los Angeles deserved this one 54% of the time. Saros stopped all 30 shots anyway, saving 2.9 goals more than the shots deserved, and Nashville left Crypto.com Arena with a 3-0 win and its fifth straight.

Filip Forsberg did the scoring, and neither goal came from a spot that usually pays. His first, 5:20 into the game, was an 18% chance off a Nils Hoglander feed. His second, midway through the second period, was a 7% snap shot, again set up by Hoglander, with Brady Skjei also in on it. That one pushed Nashville's win chance from 68% to 84%. Hoglander finished with two assists without putting a shot on goal, which is its own kind of night.

The Kings had their push. They owned the third period, out-chancing Nashville 1.17 to 0.67 in expected goals, and they threw 26 hits to Nashville's nine. Nashville blocked 21 shots and Saros handled the rest. Anton Forsberg was good at the other end, 27 saves and 0.6 goals better than expected, and his best stop came on a 20% look from Ryan O'Reilly in the second. Adam Wilsby's goal into an empty net with 2:17 left ended it.

Neither power play did anything: Nashville went 0 for 4, Los Angeles 0 for 2. Shane Wright, new in Nashville after the Matthew Wood trade, put four shots on goal in 15 minutes, and Mavrik Bourque led everyone with 0.78 expected goals on five shots.

The streak is real in the sense that matters, since the Predators have had the better of the chances in four of the five. This one, though, was Saros's. Nashville gets no rest: they're in Anaheim tonight, on the second night of a back-to-back, with Roman Josi still one point from 800.
headline: Saros closes the door, Predators win five straight
